mainEntity.name: What Payload Does a Palletizing Robot Need for My Product?

acceptedAnswer.text: The robot must carry the case weight plus the end-of-arm tool, and the combined weight for multi-case picks. In household products palletizing, liquid-filled cases are dense, so weight often decides the platform: TRFCobot handles cases up to about 22 lb, TRFCompact up to about 44 lb and TRFSpeed up to about 66 lb. Heavier units are evaluated as a custom palletizer.

mainEntity.name: How Does Zero-Pressure Accumulation Work on a Case Conveyor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zero-pressure accumulation divides the conveyor into zones that stop and start independently, so waiting cases do not push against each other. When the palletizer changes a pallet, cases queue without pressure. TRFIntraflow includes zero-pressure accumulation, plus metering and gapping to release cases to the palletizer in a controlled stream.

mainEntity.name: What Is a Drop Packer and How Does Gravity Packing Work?

acceptedAnswer.text: A drop packer collates flexible packages and loads them into the case through a controlled drop, without a robot picking each unit. TRFDroppack works this way for pillow bags, pouches, flexible bags and similar packages that tolerate controlled gravity loading. It has fewer complex components and no robotic end-of-arm tool to maintain.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Case Packer and a Case Erector?

acceptedAnswer.text: A case erector forms a flat corrugated blank into an open case; a case packer loads products into that case. TRF does not sell stand-alone case erectors: TRFOnepack erects, packs and seals the case in one machine, and complete projects can include case forming and closing with TRFRapidpack, so one partner owns the flow from flat blank to sealed case.

mainEntity.name: What Automation Reduces Labor Dependency in a Household Products Plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Palletizing and case packing are usually the first steps to automate, because they are the most repetitive and physically demanding tasks after filling. A robotic palletizer takes over stacking heavy cases, a case packer takes over loading units, and accumulation reduces the stops that call people back to the line. Operators move to supervision, quality checks and changeovers.

mainEntity.name: How Is Payback Estimated for Household Products Packaging Automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the equipment replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The estimate follows the method of the A3 (Association for Advancing Automation) robot ROI calculator: the system cost, including 20 years of maintenance at 5% per year, divided by the annual net savings, which is the labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses. Household plants should also count filler uptime recovered and shorter changeovers. The payback calculator gives a first estimate.
